name: Acquisition Channel Scalability Matrix
phase: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that [Channel X] can sustainably deliver customer acquisition at targeted unit costs. We will verify this by cross-referencing industry channel benchmarks against product characteristics, and consider it validated if the channel delivers an estimated CAC:LTV ratio of ≥ 1:3 at target market scale.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Map candidate acquisition channels against ARPU tiers and the way the target users actually buy.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Drop channels that cannot carry the price point - enterprise direct sales rarely pays below $1,000 ARPU.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Build a projection matrix of saturation, cost-per-click trend and conversion assumptions per channel.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Map potential acquisition channels against ARPU tiers and user buying habits.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Eliminate channels that don't match the product's price point (e.g., enterprise direct sales forces are rarely viable for products with an ARPU under $1,000/year).

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Build a channel projection matrix comparing expected saturation points, cost-per-click trends, and estimated conversion rates.

warning.label: Channel Mirage Effect
warning.text: Traction in niche or closed communities rarely scales when broad advertising is switched on.

warningFull: Early customer acquisition traction achieved in niche communities or closed groups rarely scales efficiently once broader advertising channels are deployed.
